```{r setup, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results="hide"}
library(targets)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Helpers (also sourced by _targets.R); keep available for Quarto render.
source("R/envdata_contract.R", local = FALSE)
source("R/coverage_metrics.R", local = FALSE)
source("R/data_freshness.R", local = FALSE)

# Pipeline deps for tar_quarto()
tar_load(coverage_metrics)
tar_load(data_freshness)
tar_load(most_recent_evi_date)
```

Sources for maps and figures on this site are derived in `emma_report` from public [`eco-emma/emma_envdata`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata) GitHub Releases and the STAC catalog. This page summarizes available data, where to download it, and how to open Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs.

# Data shown on this site

| Product | What you see | Typical as-of |
|---|---|---|
| Fused EVI | Latest greenness + monthly / long-term ΔEVI on park maps (EVI layer group) | `r format(most_recent_evi_date, "%Y-%m-%d")` |
| Veld Age (years) | Continuous fire-age raster; true ages (not collapsed to 20) | `fireage` release snapshot |
| Fire History | Burn outlines (one layer; age-bin stroke colors) | `fireage` release snapshot |
| Invasives | Recent iNaturalist records in parks + 10 km buffer (small leaf markers) | `inat_data` |
| Weather | Nearest GSOD station climate when rows exist (≥2000 when published) | `weather_data` |

Multi-sensor EVI fill order: **VIIRS NOAA-20 → VIIRS S-NPP → Terra → Aqua** (first non-NA wins). NA in EVI layers means all available sensors were missing after QA.

# STAC catalog

Browse the public STAC root and VI collection for latest 16-day composites (EVI COGs by sensor):

- [STAC catalog (`catalog.json`)](`r ENVDATA_STAC_CATALOG_URL`)
- [VI collection](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/download/stac-vi/vi_collection.json)

Latest VI item id: **`r data_freshness$stac_item_id %||% "unavailable"`** · datetime **`r data_freshness$stac_datetime %||% "unavailable"`**.

# GitHub data releases

Release **tags** for common products (open a tag page for its assets):

| Tag | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`static_data`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/static_data) | Domain grid, parks, covariates |
| [`fireage`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/fireage) | `fireage_current.tif` + dated fire-age parquet |
| [`vi_modis_terra_raster`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/vi_modis_terra_raster) / [`vi_modis_aqua_raster`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/vi_modis_aqua_raster) / [`vi_viirs_raster`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/vi_viirs_raster) | 16-day VI COGs |
| [`vi_modis_parquet`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/vi_modis_parquet) / [`vi_viirs_parquet`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/vi_viirs_parquet) | Tabular EVI by `pid` |
| [`burn_modis_raster`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/burn_modis_raster) / [`burn_viirs_raster`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/burn_viirs_raster) | Monthly burn COGs |
| [`weather_data`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/weather_data) | GSOD parquet + stations |
| [`inat_data`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/inat_data) | Invasives GeoPackage |
| [`stac`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/stac) / [`stac-vi`](https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/tag/stac-vi) | STAC JSON |

Download pattern: `https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/download/<tag>/<filename>`.

# Coverage metrics {#coverage-assessment-metrics}

Domain and park coverage totals. Denominators use the 500 m domain grid.

```{r coverage-table, echo=FALSE}
domain_km2 <- coverage_metrics$domain$km2
parks_km2 <- coverage_metrics$parks_union$km2
evi_km2 <- coverage_metrics$valid_evi$km2
known_km2 <- coverage_metrics$fire_age$known_km2
cens_km2 <- coverage_metrics$fire_age$censored_km2

tribble(
  ~Metric, ~`km²`,
  "Domain area", fmt_km2(domain_km2),
  "Parks-union area", fmt_km2(parks_km2),
  "Valid latest fused EVI", fmt_km2(evi_km2),
  "Fire-age known", fmt_km2(known_km2),
  "Fire-age censored", fmt_km2(cens_km2)
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

EVI composite date: **`r format(coverage_metrics$evi_as_of, "%Y-%m-%d")`**.

`r coverage_metrics$fire_mask_note`

**Park area (VIIRS cells intersecting the park)**

```{r park-coverage-preview, echo=FALSE}
coverage_metrics$parks |>
  arrange(desc(denom_km2)) |>
  transmute(
    Park = name,
    `Park Area (km²)` = fmt_km2(denom_km2),
    `Valid EVI km²` = fmt_km2(valid_evi_km2),
    `Fire known km²` = fmt_km2(fire_known_km2),
    `Fire censored km²` = fmt_km2(fire_censored_km2)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

# Using COGs & STAC

## QGIS (recommended)

1. **COG over HTTP** — Layer → Add Layer → Add Raster Layer → protocol `HTTPS`, paste a release download URL (or `/vsicurl/` + URL in the path field on some builds). Enable the COG driver if prompted.
2. **STAC** — Install the **STAC API Browser** / **STAC** plugin (Plugins → Manage). Open the [catalog URL](`r ENVDATA_STAC_CATALOG_URL`), drill into the VI collection, and add a sensor asset (e.g. `viirs_noaa20`) as a raster.
3. Project CRS for overlays with park polygons: domain products are **EPSG:9221** (Albers); reproject or on-the-fly as needed.

### Other GIS

- **ArcGIS Pro**: Add Data → cloud / HTTPS path to the `.tif` COG; STAC via community STAC tools if installed.
- **Global Mapper / others**: open the COG URL if HTTP GeoTIFF is supported; otherwise download the asset from the release tag page.

## R

```r
library(terra)
library(sf)
# Example: latest fire-age snapshot
r <- rast(paste0(
  "https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/download/",
  "fireage/fireage_current.tif"
))
plot(r[["fire_age_days"]])
```

```r
# STAC item → asset href (pystac-like workflow with rstac if installed)
# Or read collection JSON and pick an item link, then rast(asset_href)
```

## Python

```python
import rasterio
url = (
    "/vsicurl/"
    "https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/download/"
    "fireage/fireage_current.tif"
)
with rasterio.open(url) as ds:
    print(ds.descriptions, ds.count)
```

```python
# pip install pystac
from pystac import Catalog
cat = Catalog.from_file(
    "https://github.com/eco-emma/emma_envdata/releases/download/stac/catalog.json"
)
print([c.id for c in cat.get_children()])
```
